age.evidence: C57/BL6 males at an age range of 8-12 weeks were used for behavioral experiments.

sex.evidence: adult male and female mice; C57BL/6J mice at 2 months of age, using both sexes, were used for behavior tests and imaging.

dosing.evidence: mouse head-twitch dose-response curves were recorded following intraperitoneal injection of psilocybin (Usona Institute) at doses of 0 mg/kg-1 (saline), 0.25 mg/kg-1, 0.50 mg/kg-1 and 1.00 mg/kg-1.

dosing.doses_raw: 1-500 µM mixed with Rhodamine 6G (local injection to ACC ~2 µl or intrathecal ~5 µl)
dosing.evidence: local psilocin injection (Cayman Chemical, 9003135; 1-500 µM mixed with Rhodamine 6G) to either ACC or spinal cord

dosing.doses_raw: DOI (Cayman Chemical, 13885; 1 mg/kg i.p. dose); In Fig. 7c-f DOI (0.5 mg/kg i.p.)
dosing.evidence: SNI mice received either 8-OH-DPAT (1 mg/kg-1 i.p. dose), DOI (1 mg/kg-1 i.p. dose) or DOI/DPAT... In Fig. 7b-m, SNI mice received... DOI (0.5 mg/kg-1 i.p.); local cortical application of DOI also used at 200 µM.
SNI mice received either 8-OH-DPAT (Selleck Chemicals, S8447; 1 mg/kg-1 i.p. dose); also locally applied at 200 µM to ACC.
SNI mice received either pimavanserin (Selleck Chemicals, S8183; 1 mg/kg-1 i.p. dose)... 30 min before psilocybin
WAY-100635 (Selleck Chemicals, S2663; 1 mg/kg-1 i.p. dose), a selective 5-HT1A antagonist, 30 min before receiving psilocybin

handling.evidence: Methods do not describe an explicit handling habituation protocol.

group_housing.evidence: SNI/CFA and sham controls were housed in cages with five in each cage, with ample food and water.

day_night_flipped.evidence: All mice were maintained at the University of Pennsylvania... with normal dark/light cycle

enrichment_housing.evidence: Paper mentions food and water but does not address home-cage enrichment.

assays.assay_description: 30-min recording in an Open Field chamber (25x25 cm) immediately after psilocybin injection; total head-twitches scored offline by trained observer. Dose-response across 0.25, 0.5, 1.0 mg/kg; also used to confirm pimavanserin blockade.

setup_habituation.evidence: No mention of apparatus habituation before HTR.

setup_restrain.evidence: HTR was assessed in individual animals in an Open Field chamber (25x25 cm) for 30 min

food_restriction.evidence: Standard short test in open-field chamber; no food in apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard short test; no water in apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: HTR was assessed... for 30 min immediately after psilocybin injection

sample_size.evidence: 0.5 mg/kg-1 dose produced peak HTR (n=6) as compared with 0.25 mg/kg-1 (n=6) and 1 mg/kg-1 (n=6)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin produced an inverted-U dose response in HTR; 0.5 mg/kg produced peak HTR over 30 min compared with 0.25 and 1 mg/kg. Pretreatment with pimavanserin abolished HTR.
outcomes.evidence: 0.5 mg/kg-1 dose produced peak HTR over 30 min collection window as compared with 0.25 mg/kg-1 (P<0.0001) and 1 mg/kg-1 (P=0.0153) dosed animals.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Head twitches are summed every 5 min over the first 30 min post-injection (Extended Data Fig. 2)

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded as an ethological behaviour per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Scored offline by a trained observer.

assays.assay_description: 50x50 cm arena with 25x25 cm central zone; 5-min session via ANY-maze. Total distance, centre entries, centre time measured. Used for psilocybin dose-response (Fig 1c, 30-min) and for anxiety/locomotion assessment in SNI/CFA pain cohorts on days 0/20/28/40.

setup_habituation.evidence: Methods do not state apparatus habituation prior to OFT.

setup_restrain.evidence: the animal was gently placed in the center of the arena

food_restriction.evidence: No food in arena during testing.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in arena during testing.

time_to_assay.evidence: Used acutely (0 min) for dose-response and at day 28 (24 h post-injection) and day 40 in pain cohorts.

outcomes.summary: Acute 0.5 mg/kg psilocybin reduced total distance (hypoactivity). In SNI/CFA mice, psilocybin reversed the chronic-pain-induced reductions in total distance, centre entries and centre time, with effects persisting to day 40.
outcomes.statistics: Kruskal-Wallis (22), P=0.047, Dunn's P=0.048; SNI distance P=0.0021; CFA distance P=0.0458; SNI centre time P=0.0053; CFA centre time P=0.0161
outcomes.evidence: 0.5 mg/kg-1 group shows a substantial reduction in total movement compared with vehicle controls... SNI/CFA after psilocybin treatment increased in total distance traveled, entries to the center, and time spent in the central area.

B1_num_measures.evidence: total distance traveled, entries to the center, time spent in the central zone

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Reported as totals over the 5-min session.

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotor and zone-time measures, not ethological acts.

E6_spatial.evidence: Virtual centre zone in single arena; rubric scores OFT 0.

D1_continuity.evidence: Baseline day 0, day 20, day 28, day 40 testing.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Dose-response OFT in Fig 1c used 30-min recordings; pain cohort 5-min.

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline on day 0 in pain cohort timeline (Fig 2a).

assays.assay_name: Electronic von Frey Mechanical Sensitivity Test
assays.assay_description: Electronic von Frey anesthesiometer measuring hindlimb withdrawal threshold; three trials per day averaged. Repeated across days 0, 2, 7, 12, 19, 26, 28, 40 in SNI, CFA, sham, saline, and antagonist/agonist cohorts.

application_type.evidence: Systemic i.p. psilocybin; intrathecal psilocin to lumbosacral cord; bilateral local psilocin to ACC; pharmacological antagonists/agonists (pimavanserin, WAY-100635, DOI, 8-OH-DPAT) i.p.

setup_habituation.evidence: Methods do not mention apparatus habituation prior to vF.

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals freely positioned on testing platform; no restraint described.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard short test; no food in apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard short test; no water in apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: Pre-injury baseline; multiple post-treatment timepoints including day 28 (24 h post psilocybin) and day 40.

sample_size.evidence: SNI n=30 vs sham n=22; CFA n=22 vs saline n=15; multiple antagonist/agonist subgroups n=4-6

outcomes.summary: SNI and CFA induced persistent mechanical allodynia. Single i.p. psilocybin (0.5 mg/kg) or bilateral local psilocin to ACC reversed thresholds to pre-injury levels through day 40, while intrathecal psilocin and vehicle did not. Pimavanserin and WAY-100635 pretreatments blocked psilocybin's analgesic effect; selective full agonists DOI or 8-OH-DPAT (alone or combined) did not fully reverse allodynia.
outcomes.statistics: SNI P<0.0001 days 12, 19, 26; CFA P<0.0001 days 2, 7, 12, 19, 26; bilateral ACC psilocin vs intrathecal day 28 P=1.7x10^-5; Pima vs saline P=0.003; WAY P<0.0001
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin reversed mechanical sensitivity to pre-injury levels on day 28 that persisted for the next 12 days (SNI versus sham, P>0.05 on days 28 and 40; CFA versus saline controls, P>0.05 on days 28 and 40).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Average of three trials per day.

D1_continuity.evidence: Repeated vF tracked out to 40 days.

assays.assay_description: Cylindrical glass tank (30 cm height x 20 cm diameter), 15 cm water depth, 23-25 °C, 6-min test; last 4 min analyzed for immobility via ANY-maze. Used in SNI/CFA cohorts and antagonist/agonist studies.

application_type.evidence: i.p. psilocybin; local psilocin to ACC; pimavanserin/WAY-100635/DOI/8-OH-DPAT i.p.

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were lowered gently into water and allowed to swim freely.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in tank during test.

water_restriction.evidence: Tank filled with water - animals fully immersed.

time_to_assay.evidence: FST performed 1 day after psilocybin injection (day 28) and again at day 40.

sample_size.evidence: SNI n=20; CFA n=22; VC n=5

outcomes.summary: SNI and CFA increased FST immobility, which was reversed by systemic psilocybin (and by local ACC psilocin). 5-HT2A and 5-HT1A antagonists blocked the antidepressant-like effect. DOI/8-OH-DPAT alone or combined did not replicate the effect.
outcomes.statistics: SNI P=0.00487; CFA P=8.7x10^-5; Psilocybin SNI P=0.042; CFA P=0.00011
outcomes.evidence: SNI/CFA significantly increased the time spent immobile in FST... which was later decreased by psilocybin (SNI, P=0.042; CFA, P=0.00011).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Last 4 min analyzed as a single value.

E7_social_context.evidence: Each tank separated by a divider.

assays.assay_description: Mouse suspended by tail (anti-climb cylinder around tail base), 6-min test, final 4 min analyzed for immobility via ANY-maze.

setup_restrain.evidence: The mouse is then suspended by its tail using a long piece (~15 cm) of strong adhesive tape

time_to_assay.evidence: Tested day 28, 24 h after psilocybin; also day 40.

sample_size.evidence: SNI males n=6, females n=4; CFA males n=5, females n=5 (Extended Data Fig. 3b)

outcomes.summary: SNI/CFA increased TST immobility; psilocybin reversed this and effects persisted to day 40. DOI alone modestly reduced immobility, while 8-OH-DPAT and DOI+8-OH-DPAT did not.
outcomes.statistics: SNI P=0.00267; CFA P<0.0001; Psilocybin SNI P=0.00066; CFA P<0.0001; DOI P=0.0285
outcomes.evidence: Immobility time increased postinjury (SNI P=0.00267; CFA P<0.0001) and decreased after psilocybin treatment (SNI P=0.00066; CFA P<0.0001).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Final 4 min analyzed as a single value.

assays.assay_description: Plus-shaped maze with two open and two closed arms; 5-min test; time in open arm measured via ANY-maze.

application_type.evidence: i.p. psilocybin; bilateral local psilocin to ACC; pimavanserin/WAY-100635/DOI/8-OH-DPAT i.p.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice placed in the center and allowed to explore freely.

time_to_assay.evidence: Day 28, 24 h after psilocybin; also day 40.

sample_size.evidence: SNI n=20, sham n=12, VC n=5

outcomes.summary: SNI/CFA decreased open-arm time; psilocybin reversed this and effects persisted to day 40. Pimavanserin and WAY-100635 pretreatment blocked the effect. Bilateral ACC psilocin did not improve EPM open-arm time; selective full agonists also failed.
outcomes.statistics: SNI P=0.00019; CFA P=6.6x10^-7; Psilocybin SNI P=0.0095; CFA P=0.0022
outcomes.evidence: SNI/CFA induced a significant decrease in open arm time which was reversed by psilocybin administration (SNI, P=0.0095; CFA, P=0.0022).

E2_shelter.evidence: Closed arms do not count as shelter per rubric.

assays.assay_description: 45x30x27 cm box with covered dark third and lit two-thirds connected by 7.5x7.5 cm opening; time in light compartment recorded for 10 min via ANY-maze.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mouse gently placed in the opening, free to move.

time_to_assay.evidence: Tested day 28 (24 h after psilocybin) and day 40.

outcomes.summary: Time in light compartment decreased post-injury and returned to pre-injury levels after psilocybin in SNI but not in CFA mice.
outcomes.evidence: Time in light compartment decreases postinjury but returns to pre-injury levels after psilocybin injection in SNI but not in CFA mice.

E6_spatial.evidence: Two enclosed compartments connected by opening.

assays.assay_description: Two-chamber CPP with distinct visual cues + neutral center. Pre-conditioning 15-min free exploration; conditioning sessions 30 min in each chamber (saline vs psilocybin paired); post-test 15-min free exploration recorded via ANY-maze.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (0.5 mg/kg i.p.) paired with one chamber.

setup_habituation.evidence: Preconditioning phase with free exploration to establish baseline.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in chambers during recordings.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in chambers during recordings.

time_to_assay.evidence: Test day is one day following conditioning day.

outcomes.summary: Both SNI and CFA mice developed a significant preference for the psilocybin-paired chamber, while sham/saline controls did not.
outcomes.evidence: Total time spent in chamber B (psilocybin-paired chamber) increases following psilocybin injection in SNI and CFA mice (SNI, P=0.0022; CFA, P=0.0198).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Time in chamber B, preference index, preference score reported.

B5_social.evidence: Individual testing, drug- (not social-) conditioned CPP.

E6_spatial.evidence: Two chambers with partition + neutral chamber.

D1_continuity.evidence: Pre-conditioning, conditioning, and post-test sessions recorded.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Pre-conditioning, conditioning day, and test day.

assays.assay_description: Accelerating rotarod (1-45 rpm over 80 s, total 180 s), 3 trials averaged. Latency to fall measured before injury (day 0), day 20, day 28 (post-psilocybin), and day 40.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mouse placed on rotating rod, freely moving until fall.

time_to_assay.evidence: Day 28, 24 h after psilocybin; also day 40.

sample_size.evidence: SNI n=10, sham n=11, CFA n=10, saline n=10

outcomes.summary: Latency to fall decreased post-SNI/CFA and was rapidly restored after psilocybin on day 28, persisting to day 40.
outcomes.statistics: SNI P=7.9x10^-5; CFA P=1.6x10^-8 (one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni)
outcomes.evidence: Latency to fall decreases post-injury in (c) SNI and (f) CFA conditions, then increases post-psilocybin injection on day 28.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Motor coordination, no learning measure reported.

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline day 0 in trajectories (Extended Data Fig 4).

judge_notes: Merged candidate-specific entries for different pharmacological manipulations (psilocybin, local psilocin, DOI, 8-OH-DPAT, pimavanserin, WAY-100635) into the underlying behavioural assays (vF, FST, TST, EPM, OFT). The rubric treats different drug/route manipulations of the same paradigm as ONE assay; per-assay application_type set to 'multiple' where applicable.
Dropped non-behavioural readouts present in candidate outputs (two-photon calcium imaging in ACC, cFos immunostaining), per rubric exclusions for neural recordings and histology.
HTR scored B2=Yes because Extended Data Fig. 2 shows head twitches summed in 5-min bins over 30 min (within-session temporal dynamics).
Added dosing entries for 8-OH-DPAT, pimavanserin, and WAY-100635 that candidates missed; these are pharmacological tools but were administered to behavioural subjects.
OFT D2 set to 1 (15-60 min) because the dose-response OFT in Fig. 1c used a 30-min recording window, even though the chronic-pain OFT used 5 min; the longest session governs D2.
